title: How to Compare Commercial Leases: A Newcastle Business Checklist
excerpt: Put each proposal on the same basis before comparing totals. Record confirmed terms, uncertainty and transition costs so a headline rent does not become the whole decision.
author: Joe Kelley
metaDescription: Compare commercial lease options using consistent rent, incentives, outgoings, FitOut and exit assumptions. Prepare a useful Newcastle tenant-side decision brief.
body:
## How do you compare two commercial lease proposals?

Use the same comparison period, cost categories and assumptions for each option. Separate scheduled rent, incentives, other occupancy costs and the expenditure needed to enter or leave the premises. Record what is confirmed and what still needs checking.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, the comparison also needs to explain whether each property supports the actual workplace brief. A lower rent measure alone does not establish the better premises or business outcome.

## Establish the basis before entering figures

Gather the proposed terms, available outgoings information, incentive details, floor-area basis, review arrangements and relevant dates. Ask your solicitor to clarify the obligations and proposed wording. Have your accountant or other appointed adviser review financial and tax assumptions where needed.

**Helpful tip:** label each input as documented, proposed, quoted, estimated or unknown. Do not fill an information gap with an unverified market average.

## Keep comparable cost categories visible

| Category | Information to record | Check before comparing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rent | Schedule, period, review assumptions and floor-area basis | Does the figure already reflect rent-free periods? |
| Incentives | Proposed benefit, conditions, timing and documentation | Has it already been deducted elsewhere? |
| Outgoings and other recurring costs | Available schedules and stated inclusions/exclusions | Are both options on the same cost and GST basis? |
| Initial workplace expenditure | FitOut, furniture, technology and moving scope | Is a contribution shown against rent or against project cost? |
| Existing lease exit | Clarified obligations and scoped estimates | Which amounts remain uncertain? |
| Delivery and business fit | Access, work required, dependencies and operating needs | Can the premises support the intended activities? |

A gross or net lease label is a starting point for questions, not a complete list of inclusions. Check the actual proposal and the basis of each figure.

## Compare rent and incentives without double counting

An incentive-adjusted rent calculation can be useful when its method and assumptions are stated. It should not be described as the total cost of occupying the space or automatically treated as the actual rent cash payments.

If a rent schedule already removes rent-free months, do not subtract them again. If a landlord contribution is applied against the FitOut budget, do not also deduct the same contribution from a combined occupancy total through an adjusted rent figure.

**Helpful tip:** retain a reconciliation from the headline schedule to the adjusted figure. Show the actual payment timing separately from any average used for comparison.

[See the worked incentive-adjusted rent example](/blog/net-effective-rent-commercial-lease-explained)

## Model reviews and uncertainty explicitly

Ask your solicitor to explain the proposed review wording and conditions. Record the assumptions used for future rent and other changing costs. A scenario is not a forecast guarantee or confirmation of a future market review.

Use the same period for each option, and identify where a different term or delivery date makes a simple total difficult to compare. Consider the cash needed during the transition as well as the full-period total.

**Helpful tip:** keep a base scenario and a list of unresolved inputs rather than presenting one precise total as settled fact.

## Connect the lease decision with workplace delivery

Include the likely works, furniture, technology, move and any overlap between sites. Ask the appointed advisers to assess the actual premises, landlord requirements and relevant approval pathway before assuming the workplace will be ready on a particular date.

YOS can connect the tenant-side brief with [client-side FitOut project management](/office-fitout), where agreed. Appointed contractors carry out construction and trade work; project responsibilities and scope are confirmed separately.

[Prepare the FitOut budget scope](/blog/office-fitout-cost-guide-australia-2026)

[Clarify make-good scope and budget inputs](/blog/make-good-obligations-commercial-lease-cost)

## Use tools as planning aids

The [lease comparison tool](/resources/lease-comparison) helps organise inputs. Check its scope, calculations and assumptions, and record anything outside the tool separately. A tool output is not a legal review, valuation or project-specific quote.

YOS supports the agreed commercial workstream. Market comparisons need their evidence, date and limitations explained; a quoted asking rent is not the same as an evidenced completed transaction.

## Bring the comparison to the next conversation

[Explore Newcastle tenant representation](/tenant-rep/newcastle), [compare Tenant Rep packages](/tenant-rep#packages) or [send your leasing enquiry](#blog-contact-form) with the proposals and questions you have.

For a current lease, [start a free Lease Health Check](/lease-health-check). Uploading your current lease is optional, and further advisory work is scoped separately. Your solicitor advises on legal terms and documents.

## Further guidance

The linked NSW leasing guidance includes retail-specific context; do not assume those rules apply to every office or industrial lease. Ask your solicitor about your premises. RICS explains the need to assess and adjust comparable evidence in professional valuation work.

[NSW Small Business Commissioner: leasing costs](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/help/common-questions/understanding-the-costs-of-leasing)
